ai.description: Nanorana ercepeae is a small frog reaching 30–40 mm. It is brown with dark mottling and a pale vertebral stripe. Key features include a granular back and distinct, enlarged toe tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana ercepeae* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, prominent glandular folds on its back, which are absent or less defined in other *Nanorana* species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana ercepeae* inhabits high-altitude, fast-flowing mountain streams within evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Torrent Paa Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, fast-flowing streams it inhabits.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana ercepeae* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in mountain streams. It breeds during the monsoon season, typically depositing small clutches under submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana ercepeae* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting high-altitude streams in the Nilgiri and Anaimalai hills at elevations above 1,500m.
ai.callDescription: The Torrent Paa Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in its rocky, montane habitat.
